proposition.claim: For threshold-admissible navigable points the obstacle preference is min–max normalized, but Eq.(3) uses its zero value as the final exclusion mask. Target-distance normalization also divides by its range without a stated tie rule.

repair.content: Separate the mask \(s(n)=\mathbf1\{d_o(n)\ge\tau_o\}\) from preference. Let \(q\) be inverse target normalization with an explicit common value when distances tie, and set \(\widehat a_f=s\,\operatorname{clip}(q,0.1,1)\). The positive clipped factor makes zero equivalent to raw threshold exclusion. This restores only that property, not collision-free planning.
